core_question: Should OmniLogistics proceed with the full launch of Project SkyNet in Q4 2026, or should it delay to address compliance and fleet issues?
central_thesis: The storyline should be led by the strongest public evidence, then translated into management choices.
narrative_focus: Evidence is densest around: market, cost, adoption, funding
structure_logic: Open with the executive decision, show source-backed data exhibits, then move through business implications, risks and action gates.

OmniLogistics is allocating $45.5 million in capital expenditure for "Project SkyNet," our autonomous drone delivery initiative in urban centers.
This represents a 25% increase from our initial Q1 projections due to faster-than-expected technological advancements in obstacle avoidance systems.
The break-even point for this capital investment is estimated at 18 months post-launch, assuming a minimum daily delivery volume of 150,000 packages across our top 5 urban markets.

hypotheses_to_test.hypothesis: H1: The projected 35% cost reduction and 18-month break-even are achievable given the current capital allocation and market conditions.
H2: Consumer concerns about noise and privacy can be sufficiently mitigated by deploying Whisper-Prop and camera shuttering, maintaining the 68% acceptance rate.
H3: The regulatory weight limit (25 lbs) will force a fleet mix shift to Swift-Class drones, potentially reducing payload capacity and affecting delivery volume targets.
H4: External market benchmarks (e.g., competitor drone delivery costs, regulatory trends) will validate or challenge the internal financial projections.
H5: The 150,000 packages/day threshold is feasible across top 5 urban markets given consumer willingness to pay and operational constraints.

market_sizing_logic.formula: Total demand pool x serviceable segment share x reachable geography/use-case share
known_limitations: High-level market size can include demand that is not serviceable.

market_sizing_logic.formula: Potential customers x usage per customer x price/ARPU x adoption rate
known_limitations: Customer and price definitions must use the same scope.

market_sizing_logic.formula: Target customer pool x pilot rate x conversion rate x expansion rate
known_limitations: Early case studies may not represent scaled adoption.

market_sizing_logic.formula: Customer cost/revenue pool x improvement rate x supplier value-capture rate
known_limitations: Value-capture rate usually needs primary research.

market_sizing_logic.formula: Available capacity x utilization x unit price
known_limitations: Announced capacity is not the same as deliverable capacity.

charting_rule: Charts may use only evidence_ledger values, dates, source counts or same-unit comparable values tied to public URLs.
exhibit_narrative_rule: Every exhibit must be embedded in the section argument: prose sets up the management question before the exhibit and interprets the implication after it; never stack exhibits without prose.
